subject: Media Literacy
title: Beauty Standards and Advertising
description: A 60-second lesson on Beauty Standards and Advertising.

hook.text: Before 1995, there was no word for 'fat' in Fiji. Then TV arrived with Western ads. Eating disorders followed.

buildup.text: Advertising creates and reinforces beauty standards by showing idealized bodies as normal and desirable.

discovery.text: Studies link advertising exposure to body dissatisfaction, low self-esteem, and eating disorders.

twist.text: The beauty industry profits from insecurity. If you felt good about yourself, you'd buy fewer products.

climax.text: Advertising doesn't show you beauty. It shows you a standard you can never reach — then sells you the attempt.

punchline.text: They profit from the gap between you and impossible.

quiz.question: How does advertising benefit from beauty insecurity?
options: Insecure consumers buy more products to try to meet impossible standards
Beauty ads only target confident people
